title: Fast classical simulation algorithms for free-fermion dynamics with magic input
authors: Jiwon Heo, Oliver Reardon-Smith, Michał Oszmaniec, Zoltán Zimborás, Changhun Oh
abstract: The classical cost of simulating free-fermion (matchgate) circuits depends on both the input state and the computational task. We develop classical algorithms for circuits with non-Gaussian inputs, addressing exact sampling and both additive-error and exact estimation of expectation values. For inputs consisting of $n$ copies of the four-mode magic state, we give exact sampling algorithms, generalizing the Clifford and Clifford algorithm for Boson sampling, for passive and active free-fermion dynamics with worst-case arithmetic cost $O(2^n)$ per sample, without any multiplicative polynomial prefactor. The passive algorithm enables an exact simulation of the non-interacting regime of a recent trapped-ion experiment. We also extend recently developed additive-error estimation of number correlators and related observables from passive to active dynamics with runtime polynomial in $n$ and the inverse additive-error, for input states formed by products of $n$ four-mode even parity states. Our estimator uses a Gaussian-state decomposition adapted to each sampled state to control its second moment. This includes estimation of individual output probabilities. Finally, we show that for even-parity product inputs composed of constant-size blocks, expectation values of Majorana monomials of logarithmic weight can be computed exactly in polynomial time, improving on prior Majorana propagation-style algorithms with quasi-polynomial runtime. The exact algorithm processes the input blocks by dynamic programming, sharing calculations across subsets of Majorana factors. Our suite of algorithms provide classical benchmarks for fermionic quantum simulations across a broad spectrum of computational tasks.
summary: This paper presents advanced classical algorithms to simulate free-fermion dynamics, particularly when the initial state is non-Gaussian. It achieves efficient computation for sampling the output state and estimating various expectation values by exploiting the block-product structure of the input. These results offer significant classical benchmarks for simulating fermionic quantum circuits relevant to trapped-ion quantum computing.
main_problem: Developing fast classical simulation algorithms for free-fermion dynamics, especially when the input state is non-Gaussian.
main_result: The authors provide exact sampling algorithms for free-fermion dynamics with input states composed of magic states, achieving polynomial time for certain expectation values and improving upon prior quasi-polynomial runtimes.
method: The work develops specialized classical algorithms leveraging Gaussian state decompositions, dynamic programming, and recursive sampling theorems tailored for block-product input states.
model_or_system: The focus is on free-fermion circuits governed by quadratic Hamiltonians, simulating dynamics applied to input states formed by products of four-mode magic states, relevant to trapped-ion experiments.
key_observables: Full output distribution (Fock basis samples), number correlators, and expectation values of Majorana monomials.
important_parameters: The input state structure (products of even-parity blocks), the desired accuracy ($\epsilon$), and the failure probability ($\delta$).
main_assumptions: The algorithms assume the input blocks are pure and possess even parity; the additive-error runtimes exclude a one-time polynomial-time preprocessing step.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes reference a TABLE I summarizing various algorithm runtimes for different tasks (Sampling, Expectation value, Overlap).
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops algorithms for three tasks: exact sampling, expectation value computation, and additive-error estimation, building upon the block-product structure of the input state and utilizing advanced techniques like Gaussian decomposition and dynamic programming.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, efficient classical benchmarks for simulating complex fermionic quantum processes, directly impacting the feasibility assessment of quantum hardware simulations.

Its classical action deletes a uniformly chosen occupied output mode, and recovery adds one mode using parent probabilities. (b) The active channel E interchanges the two parity sectors without reducing their dimension. Its classical action flips a uniformly chosen output bit; recovery chooses among the M bit-flipped parent outcomes. For the magic-block inputs, progress of the active recursion is measured by the number g of intact non-Gaussian blocks, rather than by the dimension of the Hilbert space.
